blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (No way to turn Paylane off or fall back to Stripe) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Closing the Stripe account removes the redeploy rollback too) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-3 (Settlement worker has no health, metrics or failure alert) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The Stripe client is deleted and replaced by the Paylane client in the same
release. There is no switch between the two: keeping both would double the
code to maintain.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: All traffic moves at deploy
findings.recommendation: Keep the Stripe client behind a configuration switch (or a percentage flag) selecting the provider, so an operator can send traffic back to Stripe without a release; remove it in a later change once Paylane is proven.
findings.title: No way to turn Paylane off or fall back to Stripe

findings.evidence: The Stripe account is closed the day after the release.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: All traffic moves at deploy
findings.recommendation: Keep the Stripe account open until Paylane has run through a defined observation period (for example several settlement cycles without incident), and state that exit criterion in the design.
findings.title: Closing the Stripe account removes the redeploy rollback too

findings.evidence:
A new worker, `settlement-worker`, runs at 02:00, fetches the day's Paylane
payments and matches them to orders. It runs as a Kubernetes CronJob and
writes its result to the database.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: A worker settles payments nightly
findings.recommendation: Specify how a failed or missed run is detected and alerted (job failure / last-success timestamp metric, counts of payments fetched, matched and unmatched, a start/end log with run id), and add a scenario for "the worker fails".
findings.title: Settlement worker has no health, metrics or failure alert

findings.evidence: Every card payment SHALL be authorized and captured through Paylane once the change is deployed.
findings.location: specs/payments/spec.md#Requirement: Card payments go through Paylane
findings.recommendation: State a timeout on every Paylane call (checkout and worker), bounded retries with backoff only on idempotent operations, and an idempotency key on capture so a retry cannot charge twice.
findings.title: No timeout or retry policy for Paylane calls

findings.evidence:
- **WHEN** Paylane declines the card
- **THEN** the customer sees that the payment was declined
findings.recommendation: Add a scenario for Paylane being unavailable or returning an error (timeout, 5xx, auth failure) — what the customer sees and what is logged, as structured fields with the order id and Paylane reference and no card data or API key.
findings.title: Paylane errors other than a decline are not specified

findings.recommendation: State that the Paylane URL and API key are read from environment / Kubernetes secrets for both checkout and the worker, and add the secret to the manifests task.
findings.title: Paylane credentials and endpoint configuration are unplanned
